questions.stem: What is the main cause of the increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide levels?

options.text: Increased animal respiration
Volcanic eruptions only
Burning fossil fuels and deforestation
Increased photosynthesis

questions.explanation: The main causes of increased atmospheric CO2 are burning fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas) for energy and deforestation (removing trees that absorb CO2). These human activities have significantly disrupted the carbon cycle.

questions.stem: What is acid rain primarily caused by?

options.text: Methane dissolving in rainwater
Ozone dissolving in rainwater
Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides dissolving in rainwater
Carbon dioxide dissolving in rainwater

questions.explanation: Acid rain is primarily caused by sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides released from burning fossil fuels. These gases dissolve in rainwater to form sulfuric acid and nitric acid, which damage forests, lakes, and buildings.

options.text: The destruction of the ozone layer
Excessive enrichment of water with nutrients, causing algal blooms and oxygen depletion
The release of toxic chemicals into the air
The introduction of invasive species

questions.explanation: Eutrophication occurs when excess nutrients (usually from fertiliser runoff or sewage) enter waterways, causing algal blooms. When the algae die, decomposing bacteria use up oxygen, leading to the death of aquatic organisms.

options.text: It increases biodiversity by creating open spaces
It has no effect on biodiversity
It only affects plant species, not animals
It reduces biodiversity by destroying habitats

questions.explanation: Deforestation reduces biodiversity by destroying habitats. When forests are removed, the organisms that lived there lose their homes, food sources, and breeding grounds. This can lead to species extinction, especially for specialist species.

options.text: The cooling of the Earth due to pollution blocking sunlight
The warming of the Earth due to greenhouse gases trapping heat in the atmosphere
The process of growing plants in greenhouses
The formation of holes in the ozone layer

questions.explanation: The greenhouse effect is the warming of the Earth caused by greenhouse gases (CO2, methane, water vapour) in the atmosphere trapping heat that would otherwise escape into space. Human activities have enhanced this natural effect.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a consequence of global warming?

options.text: Decreased sea levels
All species becoming stronger and healthier
Decreased frequency of extreme weather events
Ice caps melting, leading to rising sea levels and habitat loss

questions.explanation: Global warming causes ice caps and glaciers to melt, leading to rising sea levels, flooding of coastal areas, and loss of habitats. It also causes changes in weather patterns, coral bleaching, and shifts in species distributions.

questions.stem: What is meant by overexploitation of resources?

options.text: Not using any natural resources
Using resources at a sustainable rate
Using resources faster than they can be replenished
Recycling all waste materials

questions.explanation: Overexploitation means using resources faster than they can be naturally replenished. Examples include overfishing, deforestation, and excessive hunting. This leads to depletion of resources and loss of biodiversity.
